safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies fever, bowel or urinary symptoms, and appetite is maintained.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes appetite/eating-drinking OK but does not document explicit denials of fever, bowel symptoms, or urinary symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting documented negative review-of-systems elements (no fever, bowel, or urinary symptoms) reduces clarity around systemic illness/infection and can broaden unnecessary differential or follow-up questioning. In this context of chronic hand dermatitis, the likelihood of direct harm is low but it can contribute to minor diagnostic/triage inefficiency.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of Type 2 diabetes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Type 2 diabetes history is not included in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document Type 2 diabetes is clinically important because diabetes affects skin integrity, infection risk, wound healing, and may change threshold for evaluating secondary infection or complications. Missing this comorbidity can lead to suboptimal assessment and management decisions.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Metformin use is not included in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting metformin from the medication list degrades medication reconciliation and can contribute to prescribing errors, interaction oversight, or incomplete understanding of chronic disease control. While it may not change topical dermatitis treatment directly, it is still a meaningful safety gap.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: NKDA is not documented in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting NKDA leaves allergy status unknown in the record, which can delay prescribing or increase the chance of an inappropriate medication being given without confirming allergies. Allergy documentation is a core medication-safety element even when current treatment is topical.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a family history of Type 2 diabetes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Family history of type 2 diabetes is not included in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Family history of Type 2 diabetes is generally a longer-term risk/screening factor and is unlikely to affect immediate management of contact dermatitis. Its omission is therefore unlikely to cause near-term clinical harm.
